questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the exact order of initialization when a Java class with a superclass is instantiated?

options.A: Child static blocks -> Parent static blocks -> Parent instance blocks/constructors -> Child instance blocks/constructors
options.B: Parent static blocks -> Child static blocks -> Parent instance blocks/constructors -> Child instance blocks/constructors
options.C: Parent instance blocks -> Child instance blocks -> Parent static blocks -> Child static blocks
options.D: Parent constructor -> Child constructor -> Parent static blocks -> Child static blocks

questions.explanation: Static initializers run top-down from parent to child class loading; then parent instance blocks/constructor run before child instance blocks/constructor.

options.B: Object

questions.explanation: Method overloading resolution happens at compile time based on reference type (Parent), which only sees show(Object). Subclass method show(String) overloads, not overrides, so p.show("hello") calls show(Object).

questions.subject: Java

options.B: Number

questions.explanation: In bounded generic parameters (<T extends Number>), type erasure replaces T with its first bound (Number) in the compiled bytecode.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: If two objects are equal according to the equals(Object) method, what MUST be true regarding their hashCode() values?

options.A: Their hash codes must be different.
options.B: Their hash codes must be equal.
options.C: Their hash codes may or may not be equal.
options.D: Their hash codes must both be zero.

questions.explanation: The equals/hashCode contract states that if two objects are equal, calling hashCode() on each must produce the same integer result.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What happens if an object's hashCode() changes while it is stored as a key in a HashMap?

options.A: The HashMap automatically updates its bucket index.
options.B: The key becomes unretrievable via map.get() because it hashes to a different bucket.
options.D: The entry is moved to the rehash list.

questions.explanation: HashMap computes bucket index from hashCode(). Mutating a key's field that affects hashCode makes map.get() search the wrong bucket, rendering it unretrievable.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the effect of calling Thread.yield() in Java?

options.A: It causes the thread to sleep for a specified duration.
options.B: It gives a hint to the thread scheduler that the current thread is willing to yield its current use of a processor.
options.D: It releases all acquired object locks.

questions.explanation: Thread.yield() signals the scheduler that the calling thread is willing to yield processor time, though the scheduler may ignore this hint.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What lock is acquired when a thread executes a static synchronized method?

options.A: The lock on 'this' instance
options.B: The lock on the Class object (Class.class)
options.D: No lock is acquired for static methods

questions.explanation: Static synchronized methods acquire the monitor lock associated with the Class object for that class.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which four conditions are necessary for a deadlock to occur in a multithreaded application?

options.A: Mutual exclusion, Hold and wait, No preemption, Circular wait
options.B: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability
options.C: Race condition, Livelock, Starvation, Priority inversion

questions.explanation: Coffman's four conditions for deadlock are Mutual Exclusion, Hold and Wait, No Preemption, and Circular Wait.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What visibility guarantee does the 'volatile' keyword provide in Java?

options.A: It guarantees atomic execution of multi-step operations like count++
options.B: It guarantees that reads and writes to the volatile variable go directly to main memory, establishing a happens-before relationship
options.C: It prevents a variable from being Garbage Collected
options.D: It locks the object instance whenever accessed

questions.explanation: Volatile ensures visible updates across threads by forcing reads/writes directly from/to main memory and preventing reordering.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which JVM memory region is shared across all threads and stores object instances?

options.A: Program Counter (PC) Register
options.B: JVM Stack

questions.explanation: Heap memory is shared by all threads and stores all Java object instances and arrays.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is Metaspace in Java 8 and later?

options.A: The garbage collector region for young generation
options.B: Off-heap native memory used to store class metadata, replacing PermGen
options.C: Thread stack space allocated for local variables
options.D: A cached pool for String literals

questions.explanation: Metaspace replaced PermGen in Java 8 to store class metadata in off-heap native memory.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the difference between map() and flatMap() in Java Streams?

options.A: map() is for parallel streams; flatMap() is for sequential streams
options.B: map() produces one output element per input element; flatMap() flattens streams of streams into a single stream
options.C: map() is terminal; flatMap() is intermediate

questions.explanation: flatMap() applies a 1-to-many mapping function that returns streams, then flattens those streams into a single composite stream.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Is a Java Stream reusable after a terminal operation has executed on it?

options.A: Yes, as many times as needed
options.B: No, an IllegalStateException will be thrown if operated upon again
options.C: Yes, but only for read-only operations
options.D: Yes, if mark() and reset() are used

questions.explanation: Streams are single-use; calling any operation after a terminal operation throws IllegalStateException.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which of the following describes a 'pure function' in functional programming?

options.A: A function that modifies global static variables
options.B: A function whose return value depends only on its arguments and has no side effects
options.C: A function that throws checked exceptions

questions.explanation: A pure function produces identical outputs for identical inputs without mutating state or causing side effects.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of inserting elements into a standard HashMap?

options.B: O(log N) in Java 8+ when buckets treeify, or O(N) prior to treeification

questions.explanation: In Java 8+, hash collisions turn buckets into Red-Black trees with O(log N) worst-case, whereas linked list buckets were O(N).

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the result of adding duplicate elements to a HashSet in Java?

options.A: Throws DuplicateKeyException
options.B: The add() method returns false and the collection remains unchanged

questions.explanation: HashSet.add() returns false if the element was already present, leaving the set unchanged.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the fundamental difference between Callable<V> and Runnable in Java?

options.A: Runnable can return a result; Callable cannot
options.B: Callable can return a result and throw checked exceptions; Runnable returns void and cannot throw checked exceptions
options.C: Runnable runs on a new thread; Callable runs on the main thread

questions.explanation: Callable's call() method returns V and throws Exception; Runnable's run() returns void and cannot throw checked exceptions.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What does CompletableFuture.thenCombine() do in Java asynchronous programming?

options.A: Executes two futures sequentially
options.B: Combines results of two independent CompletableFutures when both complete using a BiFunction
options.D: Cancels both futures if one fails

questions.explanation: thenCombine executes two independent futures in parallel and applies a function when both finish.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the purpose of the Java Virtual Machine (JVM) Execution Engine JIT (Just-In-Time) compiler?

options.A: To check syntax errors at compile time
options.B: To compile frequently executed bytecode (hotspots) directly into native machine code at runtime
options.C: To compress bytecode into JAR files
options.D: To verify bytecode safety before execution

questions.explanation: JIT compiles heavily executed bytecode into native machine code to boost runtime performance.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Why is 'new T()' invalid in Java Generics?

options.A: Generics are private by default
options.B: Type erasure removes type information T at runtime, making exact type instantiation impossible without reflection

questions.explanation: Due to type erasure, the exact class of T is unknown at runtime, preventing direct instantiation via 'new T()'.

questions.subject: Java

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: If you override equals() in a custom class, why MUST you also override hashCode()?

options.A: To allow the object to be garbage collected
options.B: To satisfy contract required by hash-based collections like HashMap and HashSet
options.C: To enable comparison using the == operator

questions.explanation: Failing to override hashCode causes equal objects to produce different hash codes, breaking Hash-based collections.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the difference between ReentrantLock and the synchronized keyword?

options.A: ReentrantLock supports lock polling, fairness policies, and interruptible locks, whereas synchronized is a block-level keyword
options.B: synchronized is faster in all cases

questions.explanation: ReentrantLock provides advanced features like trylock(), fairness, and condition variables.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: How does CopyOnWriteArrayList achieve thread safety?

options.A: By locking the whole array for every read and write
options.B: By creating a fresh copy of the underlying array upon every write operation
options.C: By using lock-free CAS atomic integers for indexing
options.D: By wrapping all methods in synchronized blocks

questions.explanation: Mutative operations (add, set, remove) make a underlying array copy, allowing lock-free reads.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What will happen when evaluating an infinite stream using reduce() without a limiting operation?

options.A: It returns Optional.empty()
options.B: It hangs indefinitely or results in OutOfMemoryError / StackOverflowError
options.D: It automatically limits evaluation to 1000 items

questions.explanation: Terminal operations like reduce() attempt to process all stream elements; on an infinite stream without limit(), it runs indefinitely.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is a 'happens-before' relationship in the Java Memory Model (JMM)?

options.A: A guarantee that memory writes by one thread are visible to another thread's reads under specific synchronization actions
options.B: A constraint forcing threads to run synchronously

questions.explanation: Happens-before guarantees that memory writes made by one statement are visible to another statement across threads.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which method of Thread is safe to stop thread execution without corrupting shared lock states?

options.A: Thread.stop()
options.B: Setting a volatile flag / calling Thread.interrupt()

questions.explanation: Thread.stop(), suspend(), and resume() are deprecated due to lock leaks; flag/interrupt cooperative cancellation is safe.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is Garbage Collection 'PhantomReference' used for?

options.A: To keep an object strongly reachable in memory
options.B: To perform post-mortem cleanup actions after an object has been finalized and reclaimed
options.C: To create soft caches for bitmap graphics
options.D: To prevent garbage collection from reclaiming the object

questions.explanation: PhantomReferences are enqueued after memory reclamation to schedule post-mortem resource cleanups safely.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity for search in a ConcurrentHashMap in Java 8?

options.B: O(log N)

questions.explanation: In Java 8, treeified buckets ensure logarithmic search complexity O(log N) even under high hash collision rates.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the purpose of Sealed Classes introduced in Java 17?

options.A: To make all methods in a class final by default
options.B: To restrict which other classes or interfaces may extend or implement them
options.C: To prevent class loading over network protocols

questions.explanation: Sealed classes (and interfaces) specify explicitly via 'permits' which subclasses are allowed to extend them.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which Garbage Collector is designed for low latency by performing almost all concurrent GC work in Java 11+?

options.A: Serial GC
options.B: Parallel GC

questions.explanation: ZGC is a scalable low-latency garbage collector performing concurrent marking and compaction with sub-millisecond pause times.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the key purpose of ForkJoinPool in Java 7+?

options.A: To manage database connection pools
options.B: To execute divide-and-conquer tasks using work-stealing algorithms
options.D: To replace standard HTTP connection handlers

questions.explanation: ForkJoinPool uses work-stealing where idle threads steal tasks from busy thread queues for parallel divide-and-conquer tasks.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What occurs if you attempt to modify a collection while iterating through it using a standard Iterator (without Iterator's own remove method)?

options.A: NullPointerException
options.B: ConcurrentModificationException

questions.explanation: Fail-fast iterators detect structural modification via modCount and throw ConcurrentModificationException.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which Java 8 feature allows composing multiple Function instances together sequentially?

options.A: Function.andThen() and Function.compose()
options.B: Function.join()

questions.explanation: Function.andThen() and compose() allow chaining mathematical/functional transformations.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which statement regarding PECS (Producer Extends, Consumer Super) rule is correct?

options.A: Use ? extends T if you only read (produce) from a generic structure, and ? super T if you only write (consume) into it
options.B: Use ? super T to read elements and ? extends T to insert elements
options.C: PECS applies only to Arrays, not Generics
options.D: PECS is a memory allocation optimization strategy

questions.explanation: Producer Extends, Consumer Super governs wildcard bounds for reading vs writing generic collections.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question:
What is the output of:
List.of("a", "b", "c").stream()
    .peek(System.out::print)
    .findFirst();

options.A: a
options.B: abc

questions.explanation: Streams are evaluated short-circuiting; findFirst() requests only 1 element, so peek() processes only "a".

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is an AtomicInteger and how does it achieve thread safety without traditional locking?

options.A: It uses hardware-level Compare-And-Swap (CAS) instructions
options.B: It synchronizes all methods internally

questions.explanation: Atomic classes utilize lock-free CPU primitives like Compare-And-Swap (CAS) for atomic operations.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What happens when a subclass constructor calls super() implicitly or explicitly?

options.A: It creates two separate objects in heap memory
options.B: It initializes superclass fields within the same memory instance being constructed
options.C: It throws InstantiationException if the superclass is concrete
options.D: It resets static variables of the parent class

questions.explanation: super() delegates construction of inherited state on the same object reference currently being instantiated.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is a Race Condition in multithreaded Java applications?

options.A: A situation where threads execute too quickly for memory writeback
options.B: A condition where correctness depends on relative timing or interleaving of multiple threads accessing shared mutable state
options.C: When two threads hold locks and wait for each other
options.D: When a thread runs out of stack space

questions.explanation: Race conditions occur when concurrent execution without synchronization produces unintended outcomes dependent on timing.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the purpose of Java ClassLoader hierarchy (Bootstrap, Platform/Extension, Application)?

options.A: To optimize array allocation
options.B: To delegate class loading upwards first (Parent Delegation Model) to ensure core runtime security and avoid duplicate loading

questions.explanation: The Parent Delegation Model ensures system classes (like java.lang.Object) are loaded by bootstrap loaders rather than untrusted custom loaders.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the capacity growth behavior of Vector when it reaches capacity compared to ArrayList?

options.A: Vector doubles its size (100% growth by default), while ArrayList grows by 50% (1.5x)
options.B: Vector grows by 50%, ArrayList doubles

questions.explanation: ArrayList grows by 50% (newCapacity = oldCapacity + (oldCapacity >> 1)); Vector doubles capacity by default.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What are Record classes introduced in Java 16?

options.A: Mutable data carrier classes with public fields
options.B: Immutable data-carrier classes that automatically generate getters, equals(), hashCode(), and toString()
options.C: Database mapping entities in standard JDK

questions.explanation: Records serve as transparent, immutable data carriers with auto-generated constructor, accessors, equals, hashCode, and toString.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What happens if a class implements two interfaces containing identical default methods without overriding that method?

options.A: The first interface's method is picked automatically
options.B: The second interface's method is picked automatically
options.C: Compilation error due to method conflict

questions.explanation: Multiple default methods with identical signatures cause a compile-time conflict that must be resolved by overriding in the class.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the ThreadLocal class used for in Java?

options.A: Sharing data safely across threads without synchronization
options.B: Providing thread-scoped variables where each thread accesses its own isolated instance
options.D: Managing thread priorities in thread pools

questions.explanation: ThreadLocal maintains independent variable instances per thread, avoiding synchronization overhead for thread-isolated state.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which collector should be used with Stream collect() to partition elements into two groups based on a predicate?

options.A: Collectors.groupingBy()
options.B: Collectors.partitioningBy()

questions.explanation: Collectors.partitioningBy() splits stream elements into Map<Boolean, List<T>> based on a given Predicate.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What does the JVM command line flag '-Xmx2g' specify?

options.A: Initial Java Heap Size of 2 Gigabytes
options.B: Maximum Java Heap Size of 2 Gigabytes

questions.explanation: -Xmx sets maximum heap memory limit; -Xms sets initial heap memory limit.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which statement accurately describes 'Virtual Threads' introduced in Project Loom (Java 21)?

options.A: Lightweight user-mode threads managed by the JVM rather than OS-level kernel threads
options.B: Threads executing exclusively in virtual machines outside the JVM
options.D: Threads designed exclusively for GPU processing

questions.explanation: Virtual threads (Java 21) are lightweight, user-mode threads managed by the JVM that dramatically scale throughput for I/O bound workloads.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the function of a Semaphore in java.util.concurrent?

options.A: To coordinate barrier synchronization among a fixed set of threads
options.B: To maintain a set of permits to restrict concurrent access to a resource pool
options.C: To exchange data between two threads at a rendezvous point

questions.explanation: Semaphores manage permits to throttle/limit concurrent access to constrained resources.

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: Which class in Java standard library provides null-safe static utility methods for computing equals and hashCode?

options.A: java.util.Objects
options.B: java.util.ObjectUtils

questions.explanation: java.util.Objects provides static methods like Objects.equals(a, b) and Objects.hash(...)

questions.subject: Java
questions.question: What is the average time complexity of searching for an element in a balanced TreeSet / TreeMap in Java?

options.B: O(log N)

questions.explanation: TreeSet and TreeMap are implemented using Red-Black trees, providing O(log N) guaranteed time complexity for search, insertion, and deletion.
